knowledge:
- key_parameters: weightCol=Column name in peak file used to weight coverage or tag matrix calculations (e.g., "V5") ;; TxDb=Transcript database object (e.g., TxDb.Hsapiens.UCSC.hg19.knownGene or EnsDb) containing genomic features ;; tssRegion=A numeric vector defining the TSS flanking region, default is c(-3000, 3000) ;; annoDb=Optional annotation database (e.g., "org.Hs.eg.db") to add extra gene metadata (SYMBOL, GENENAME, etc.) ;; upstream/downstream=Flanking distances for promoter/body regions; can be absolute base pairs or relative (rel(0.2)) ;; by=Feature type to align peaks to (e.g., "gene", "5UTR", "3UTR") ;; type=Region type to profile (e.g., "start_site", "body", "end_site") ;; nbin=Number of bins for the binning method to scale regions of different lengths and speed up calculations ;; nShuffle=Number of shuffles for background null distribution in overlap enrichment testing (recommended >= 1000)
- alternatives: EnsDb (from ensembldb package) can be used as an alternative to TxDb for peak annotation, provided chromosome naming styles are matched ;; DOSE, ReactomePA, and clusterProfiler are used for downstream functional enrichment analysis of annotated genes ;; deeptools is mentioned as the conceptual source of the binning method
- when_to_use: Use when you have genomic coordinates of ChIP-seq peaks (e.g., BED files from MACS2) and want to identify nearest genes, assign genomic features (promoter, exon, intron, etc.), visualize binding profiles around TSS/gene bodies, or compare multiple ChIP-seq datasets
- pitfalls: Gene body regions shorter than the specified nbin value will be filtered out during profiling, which triggers a warning message ;; When using Ensembl-based EnsDb annotation databases, chromosome naming styles must be matched (e.g., converting Ensembl style to UCSC style using seqlevelsStyle(edb) <- "UCSC") ;; Low nShuffle values (e.g., 50) are only for quick demonstration; robust statistical testing of peak overlaps requires nShuffle of 1000 or more

workflows.name: peak_profiling_and_visualization
workflows.intent: Profile and visualize ChIP peak binding distributions around TSS or gene body regions using heatmaps and average profiles.
workflows.stages: 1. Read peak file using readPeakFile ;; 2. Plot peak coverage over chromosomes using covplot ;; 3. Retrieve tag matrix around genomic regions using getTagMatrix ;; 4. Generate heatmaps of peak binding using tagHeatmap, peakHeatmap, or peak_Profile_Heatmap ;; 5. Plot average profiles of peak binding using plotAvgProf, plotAvgProf2, or plotPeakProf2
workflows.code:
files <- getSampleFiles()
peak <- readPeakFile(files[[4]])
covplot(peak, weightCol="V5")
covplot(peak, weightCol="V5", chrs=c("chr17", "chr18"), xlim=c(4.5e7, 5e7))
data("tagMatrixList")
tagMatrix <- tagMatrixList[[4]]
tagHeatmap(tagMatrix)
peakHeatmap(peak = files[[4]], TxDb = txdb, upstream = rel(0.2), downstream = rel(0.2), by = "gene", type = "body", nbin = 800)
plotAvgProf(tagMatrix, xlim=c(-3000, 3000), xlab="Genomic Region (5'->3')", ylab = "Read Count Frequency")
plotPeakProf2(peak = peak, upstream = rel(0.2), downstream = rel(0.2), conf = 0.95, by = "gene", type = "body", nbin = 800, TxDb = txdb, weightCol = "V5",ignore_strand = F)

workflows.name: peak_annotation_and_enrichment
workflows.intent: Annotate peaks with genomic features and nearest genes, visualize annotation distributions, and perform functional enrichment analysis.
workflows.stages: 1. Annotate peaks with genomic features and nearest genes using annotatePeak ;; 2. Visualize genomic annotations using plotAnnoPie, plotAnnoBar, vennpie, or upsetplot ;; 3. Visualize distance to TSS using plotDistToTSS ;; 4. Link genomic regions to genes using seq2gene ;; 5. Perform pathway enrichment using enrichPathway
workflows.code:
peakAnno <- annotatePeak(files[[4]], tssRegion=c(-3000, 3000), TxDb=txdb, annoDb="org.Hs.eg.db")
plotAnnoPie(peakAnno)
plotAnnoBar(peakAnno)
vennpie(peakAnno)
plotDistToTSS(peakAnno, title="Distribution of transcription factor-binding loci\nrelative to TSS")
library(ReactomePA)
pathway1 <- enrichPathway(as.data.frame(peakAnno)$geneId)
head(pathway1, 2)
gene <- seq2gene(peak, tssRegion = c(-1000, 1000), flankDistance = 3000, TxDb=txdb)
pathway2 <- enrichPathway(gene)
head(pathway2, 2)
dotplot(pathway2)

workflows.name: multi_dataset_comparison
workflows.intent: Compare genomic annotations, TSS distance distributions, and binding profiles across multiple ChIP-seq datasets.
workflows.stages: 1. Plot comparative average profiles using plotAvgProf or plotPeakProf2 ;; 2. Plot comparative heatmaps using tagHeatmap ;; 3. Annotate multiple peak files using lapply and annotatePeak ;; 4. Compare genomic annotations using plotAnnoBar ;; 5. Compare TSS distance distributions using plotDistToTSS ;; 6. Compare functional profiles using compareCluster ;; 7. Visualize overlap of annotated genes using vennplot
workflows.code:
data("tagMatrixList")
plotAvgProf(tagMatrixList, xlim=c(-3000, 3000))
tagHeatmap(tagMatrixList)
peakAnnoList <- lapply(files, annotatePeak, TxDb=txdb, tssRegion=c(-3000, 3000), verbose=FALSE)
plotAnnoBar(peakAnnoList)
plotDistToTSS(peakAnnoList)
genes = lapply(peakAnnoList, function(i) as.data.frame(i)$geneId)
names(genes) = sub("_", "\n", names(genes))
compKEGG <- compareCluster(geneCluster   = genes, fun           = "enrichKEGG", pvalueCutoff  = 0.05, pAdjustMethod = "BH")
dotplot(compKEGG, showCategory = 15, title = "KEGG Pathway Enrichment Analysis")
vennplot(genes)

workflows.name: overlap_testing_and_geo_mining
workflows.intent: Test the statistical significance of overlap between ChIP-seq datasets and mine public GEO datasets for co-regulation.
workflows.stages: 1. Shuffle genomic coordinates using shuffle ;; 2. Test overlap significance using enrichPeakOverlap ;; 3. Query GEO species and genomes using getGEOspecies and getGEOgenomeVersion ;; 4. Retrieve GEO metadata using getGEOInfo
workflows.code:
p <- GRanges(seqnames=c("chr1", "chr3"), ranges=IRanges(start=c(1, 100), end=c(50, 130)))
shuffle(p, TxDb=txdb)
enrichPeakOverlap(queryPeak     = files[[5]], targetPeak    = unlist(files[1:4]), TxDb          = txdb, pAdjustMethod = "BH", nShuffle      = 50, chainFile     = NULL, verbose       = FALSE)
getGEOspecies()
getGEOgenomeVersion()
hg19 <- getGEOInfo(genome="hg19", simplify=TRUE)
head(hg19)
